# Design

Wave 0 retargets the tooling from host roles to Fly apps, fronts search from a Fly app, closes the validator attestor ports and keeps the docs on the router URL. Wave 1 makes the kernel real: settlement on the precompiles, the finality verifier bound in layerxd, the bare-host abort points fixed, the kernel image and app on Fly with its init, two Paxeer boundaries inside it, the genesis and sequencer key made inside the machine and a value loop proven through layerxctl. Wave 2 runs the kernel's boundaries, turns the existing endpoint app into the router, brings the identity service and the registry up as Fly apps and gives the TLS-only public services a plain listener for the Fly edge. Wave 3 completes the human graph inside the kernel app for the wallet identity, brings the internal services up once the human service's event listener exists and brings agentd and MCP live. Wave 4 runs in parallel over everything else and ends with the probe of every public name.

tools/bringup/check-live.sh <subcommand> follows tools/wallet/check-live.sh: one subcommand per system, one line per check printed as pass or fail with the observed value, exit 0 only when every check passes, exit 2 on usage, CHECK_LIVE_TIMEOUT per request; ssh checks use the host map and never print it; Fly checks read the app name from the app's toml and run inside a machine through flyctl ssh console; tools/bringup/check-live.test.sh exercises the argument parsing and the pass and fail lines against local fixtures.

hosts, ca, search-front, validators, kernel-app, kernel-node, kernel-value-loop, paxeer-boundary, kernel-boundaries, router, identity, internal, registry, human, agent, human-session, wallet, search, xweb-attest, xweb-attestors, archive-node, explorer, developers, relay, interop, interop-adapters, mirrors, ramp, gas, bridge, ci, hpx, rpc-nodes, rpc-placement, indexer, agent-public, names

One Fly app per service, named after the wallet fleet's pattern: router paxeer-shared-endpoint with its Redis paxeer-shared-endpoint-redis, kernel app paxeer-human-service, identity paxeer-identity, internal services paxeer-internal (process groups kms, journeys, payments, approvals and programs, each event source reached at <group>.process.paxeer-internal.internal) with its Redis paxeer-internal-redis, program registry paxeer-registry, indexer paxeer-indexer, webhooks paxeer-webhooks (process groups public and ingress), dashboard API paxeer-dashboard, dashboard web paxeer-dashboard-web, relay archive paxeer-relay-archive, interop gateway paxeer-interop, reference ramp paxeer-ramp, gas station paxeer-gas-station, bridge relayer paxeer-bridge-relayer, hpx registry paxeer-hpx-registry, search front paxeer-search-front and the x-websearch attestors paxeer-xweb-attestor-1 to paxeer-xweb-attestor-4, distinct from the wallet attestor apps paxeer-attestor-1 to -5; primary region ams, second region fra.

125: the kernel network id equals the Paxeer chain id so the kernel and its settlement chain share one number, and differs from the private testnet id 402; NetworkId is a nonzero u32 and bootstrap.sh accepts 1..4294967295. The kernel app env LAYERX_NODE_NETWORK_ID carries it, docker/kernel/init.sh and tools/bringup/kernel-genesis.sh read it from there.

Inside the kernel machine: 9401 the node endpoint, 9443 platform core, 9444 its admin plane, 9445 the receipt authority, 9446 the agent boundary, 9447 and 9448 the two Paxeer boundaries, 9449 the human service TLS listener under the internal CA for the journeys and approvals event sources, 9450 the kms on loopback, 9451 and 9452 the guarantors, 9453 the program listener, 9454 agentd; a new listener takes the next free port of this map. Reserved beyond the running set: 9455 the relay archive origin hop on the private network, 9456 the mirror publisher status listener on loopback; a new listener takes the next free port after 9456.

Each Fly app has a fly.toml beside its pod definition, or under human/wallet/deploy for the apps of the wallet fleet, and builds from its docker/ directory. Its env carries exactly the env names the pod definition declares with listen values on [::]; its secrets are [[files]] entries with a secret_name; a single-writer app mounts one volume at /data, except the hpx registry, whose image serves its node directory from /srv/hpx and mounts its volume there; a public name is an http_service on a plain listener or, for an mTLS surface, a [[services]] TCP passthrough. The kernel app's image docker/kernel is the union of docker/platform-node, platform-core, platform-authority, platform-agent-boundary, interop-mirror and human-service plus layerx-mcp on a Debian base with socat and util-linux; its init docker/kernel/init.sh replays the init containers of platform/hosted/node/deployment.yaml and then supervises every container command of that pod under its uid (4020, 4021, 4026); its volume holds /data/layerx and /data/human-state; its machine is a performance class with at least four CPUs and 16GB in the region nearest the RPC nodes by measured round trip.
